mathematical_findings: The variation bound is explicitly uniform over every finite increasing sequence in the entire real line. It imposes finite total variation without requiring the slope v to be globally integrable; ReLU is therefore included.

A finite-valued function with finite global variation is bounded. The assumed right-continuous representative is measurable and thus locally integrable, consistently giving the local absolute-continuity identity for f.

For the right-continuous representative, the interval convention mu((a,b])=v(b)-v(a) is the correct Lebesgue-Stieltjes convention. Its distributional derivative is the finite signed curvature measure.

On the real line, finite-on-compact Borel measures have the Radon regularity used here; finite global variation makes the positive and negative parts globally finite. The signed-Radon description is valid in this setting.

ReLU uses the right-continuous slope representative1 on[0,infinity) and0 below; its curvature is exactly delta0. The value chosen at zero changes no weak derivative and does not alter the thesis separate backpropagation tie convention.
Jordan parts separate positive and negative curvature, and their sum is the total-variation measure. This includes singular continuous variation as well as slope jumps.

With V(t)=|mu|((-infinity,t]) and finite endpoint slopes, the unchanged D formula gives profiles whose distributional curvatures are mu_plus and mu_minus. Their one-sided slopes lie in the same finite common bound, so the derivative-free increment criterion applies.
For ReLU, total curvature mass1 and endpoint slopes0,1 give L=1, D=ReLU, p=ReLU andq=0; the stated maximum-and-identity pair follows exactly.
